:::{#sol-left-null-space-practice}

Here

$$
\tp{\matr{A}}\vecf{y}
= \sbmat{1 & 2 \\ 2 & 4} \sbmat{2 \\ -1}
= \sbmat{2 - 2 \\ 4 - 4}
= \sbmat{0 \\ 0},
$$

so $\vecf{y}$ is in $\mathcal{N}(\tp{\matr{A}})$.
Here $\matr{A}$ equals its own [transpose](linear-algebra-matrices.qmd#def-matrix-transpose),
so $\vecf{y}$ is in $\mathcal{N}(\matr{A})$ as well.

:::
